decisions.reason: “Thought” preserves the inward muttering without a literal “to himself” phrasing.
“By virtue of” keeps the sense that noble blood was the basis of the tsars’ rule.
“Unmistakable” changes the source’s image of a vivid, clear smile.
The ellipsis character follows the required English punctuation convention.
“Eyes widened” preserves the source action in direct, natural prose.
“Swarming” naturally conveys bees tangled together, and the phrasing keeps the escalating number.
“Rising through” preserves the image of the flames emerging as the floor melts.
The relative clause keeps the sphere blazing like a tiny sun.
“Staring at it” refers clearly to the phenomenon and retains the dictator’s shock.
The source specifies that the handful of people who knew were involved; SOL drops that qualifier.
“Far beyond what it had possessed before” keeps the comparison and reads naturally.
The question retains Morgoth’s wonder at humans creating power like this.
“Expression of awe” preserves the source’s sincere amazement.
“Laughed aloud” preserves the source action; the sentence break keeps the timing clear.
The fragment completes the preceding thought while preserving the point about a human’s ambition.
The wording keeps the implication that Morgoth had already seen through everything.
“Now called Vladimir” naturally conveys that the weapon received a new name.
“Common sense and order” preserves what the Great Cataclysm overturned without adding “laws.”
Naming Russia clarifies the country meant by “the country” without changing the source’s meaning.
The source emphasizes that he and Russia alone had to survive; SOL drops “alone.”
“Despite decades of not smoking” keeps the contrast with his few drags from the cigar.
“Shook like a leaf” carries the source’s trembling-aspen image in a natural English idiom.
“Drew deeper than he ever had before” preserves the unusually deep drag.
The explicit “He spoke the name” completes the preceding sentence fragment without adding information.
The aura’s dispersal and enveloping of its master remain intact.
“Fifty megatons” accurately renders 50 Mt and retains the TNT equivalent.
The revised phrasing preserves the publicly known figures and reads naturally.
“Little Boy” correctly uses the bomb’s name without an unnecessary article.
“Displays of power” preserves the Cold War’s show-of-force sense without narrowing it to an arms race.
The source explicitly calls it a monster; SOL drops that image.
“In an instant” preserves the source’s explicit timing cue.
“Despite their fear” and “rushed … when” preserve the soldiers’ resolve and the citizens’ simultaneous flight.
The repeated “everyone” retains the source’s emphasis and remains clear.
“It all” makes clear that the heat and mingled atomic and Magic Gem energy together spread and devoured everything; SOL’s “It” has an unclear antecedent.
“Endlessly. Greedily.” directly preserves the source’s unending, voracious spread.
“His own” clearly identifies the dictator among the lives swallowed, matching the source.
“Molten metal” and the split sentences preserve the image while improving the phrasing.
“The moment” and the dash preserve the source’s timing and suspense before the next event.
The reordered sentences preserve both Morgoth’s standing among dragons and the space trembling at his fingertips.
“Compacting” is a natural rendering of the material being packed and solidified.
The source describes the castle being erected; “There it stood” changes the action to a resulting state.
Removing the unnecessary comma preserves the description without changing its meaning.
The source says the castle stood on black earth amid magically saturated air, not that it was built from air and earth.
